headline: Hong Kong's Consumer Council received 3,078 customer-service complaints in nine months, more than in all of last year, but says AI accounts for only a small part.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: the South China Morning Post headline blames AI, but the council’s figures show AI-related complaints are a small share.
importance_line: Shoppers in Hong Kong face slow or missing replies from merchants, yet AI explains only 158 of the complaints, so the story is more about service quality than about AI.
summary: The Standard (Hong Kong) reports that the Consumer Council received 3,078 customer-service complaints in the first nine months of 2026, up more than 60 percent year on year and above the 2,715 recorded in all of 2025. Council chief executive Alaina Shum Jiu-fai said AI-related complaints came to 158 cases, a relatively small share, and that the quality of human customer service remains the main problem.
notes: Pool item was South China Morning Post (403 blocked); we read The Standard, which gives the council’s figures. SCMP’s own text was not read.
